items.synopsis: On Junos SRX5000 series platforms with Services Processing Card 3 (SPC3), executing the unsupported operational command "show pfe statistics dma" causes loss of communication between the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE)…
items.description: On Junos SRX5000 series platforms with Services Processing Card 3 (SPC3), executing the unsupported operational command "show pfe statistics dma" causes loss of communication between the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) and the Routing Engine (RE), triggering a system-wide Flexible PIC Concentrator reset and resulting in a complete traffic outage.

items.description: On SRX1600 switching mode, table full error message displayed even the L2 table is not full

items.description: MAC limit Count show 65k in srx1600, but it stops learning at 28k.

items.synopsis: On SRX1600, SRX2300 and SRX4300 platforms, upon configuring "set protocols l2-learning global-mode switching" where 1G SFP is used on 10G port the port goes down after sometime causing traffic drop.
items.description: On SRX1600, SRX2300 and SRX4300 platforms, upon configuring "set protocols l2-learning global-mode switching" where 1G SFP is used on 10G port the port goes down after sometime causing traffic drop. This traffic drop is only subjected to the port where the configuration is applied, thus the other ports remains unaffected.

items.synopsis: On ACX7020 platforms, when there is the requirement for having 100 Mbps CLI (also known as Antman NPI) connection for management, this is not supported for a specific Junos version
items.description: On ACX7020 platforms, when there is the requirement for having 100 Mbps CLI (also known as Antman NPI) connection for management, this is not supported for a specific Junos version

items.description: On ACX5448 platform, a high amount of disk I/O leads to a deadlock, which triggers a panic reboot and a vmcore file is generated. During device restart, all services are temporarily unavailable.

items.description: set class-of-service host-outbound-traffic dscp-code-point was disabled on PTX in 25.4R1. Later it was enabled in 26.2R1 and backported to 25.4R2

items.synopsis: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, due to linux kernel issue, periodical sync from system time to RTC (Real-Time Communication) every 11min stops working when system time moves to backwards.
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, due to linux kernel issue, periodical sync from system time to RTC (Real-Time Communication) every 11min stops working when system time moves to backwards.

items.synopsis: On Junos EVO platforms, frequent trace file rotation may cause certain EVO applications to become unresponsive.
items.description: On Junos EVO platforms, frequent trace file rotation may cause certain EVO applications to become unresponsive.

items.synopsis: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, when a CLI(Command Line Interface) session times out, it triggers a terminal reset which clears the visible screen and scrollback buffer.
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, when a CLI(Command Line Interface) session times out, it triggers a terminal reset which clears the visible screen and scrollback buffer. As a result, users are unable to view previous command outputs.

items.synopsis: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, when both rib-sharding and the ephemeral database are enabled, committing any routing related configuration changes cause the rpd process to crash thus result in routing protocol…
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, when both rib-sharding and the ephemeral database are enabled, committing any routing related configuration changes cause the rpd process to crash thus result in routing protocol disruption and traffic impact until the routing process recovers.

items.synopsis: On Junos OS Evolved platforms that support dual Routing Engine(RE) but are operating with a single RE, NETCONF commit operations incorrectly display the "graceful-switchover is enabled, commit synchronize should be…
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms that support dual Routing Engine(RE) but are operating with a single RE, NETCONF commit operations incorrectly display the "graceful-switchover is enabled, commit synchronize should be used" warning when Graceful Routing Engine Switchover (GRES) is enabled. The warning is cosmetic, and NETCONF commit operations complete successfully despite the warning. Existing traffic forwarding and control plane operation are not affected.

items.synopsis: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with EVPN-MPLS (Ethernet VPN- Multiprotocol label switching) and VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) stitching , ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) entries learned over a VTEP (Virtual…
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with EVPN-MPLS (Ethernet VPN- Multiprotocol label switching) and VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) stitching , ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) entries learned over a VTEP (Virtual Tunnel Endpoint) interface are not refreshed by re-ARP (unicast ARP refresh) mechanism. As a result, ARP entries can age out and are temporarily removed causing intermittent traffic disruption. This issue will be restored automatically when ARP entries are re-learnt after some delay(several hundreds milli seconds).

items.synopsis: IPv6 neighbor is not switching to the correct Redundant Trunk Group (RTG) link when we bring back up the primary link after a failover scenerio.
items.description: IPv6 neighbor is not switching to the correct Redundant Trunk Group (RTG) link when we bring back up the primary link after a failover scenerio. Switching from the primary link to the standby works ok, but when switching back, the ipv6 neighbor still points to the standby link causing traffic to blackhole to that destination. Ipv4 arp works ok.

items.synopsis: On SRX1500 platform, when an SFP-T transceiver port (ge-0/0/12 to ge-0/0/15) is administratively disabled, the local interface shows down, but the link on the peer device remains up.
items.description: On SRX1500 platform, when an SFP-T transceiver port (ge-0/0/12 to ge-0/0/15) is administratively disabled, the local interface shows down, but the link on the peer device remains up. The link status of a disabled SFP-T port on SRX1500 is down, but peer remote port remains up.

items.synopsis: On SRX devices operating in a High Availability cluster with logical-systems enabled, the backup node may display fewer flow sessions than the primary node due to incomplete flow session synchronization.
items.description: On SRX devices operating in a High Availability cluster with logical-systems enabled, the backup node may display fewer flow sessions than the primary node due to incomplete flow session synchronization. Sessions that do not synchronize to the backup node are lost during a failover, resulting in service interruption for the affected flows.

items.synopsis: On Junos QFX5110, QFX5120, EX4650, EX4400, EX4100, and EX5200 platforms, when operating with EVPN-VxLAN type5 overlay ECMP at high tunnel next hop scale, the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) crash when a memory corruption…
items.description: On Junos QFX5110, QFX5120, EX4650, EX4400, EX4100, and EX5200 platforms, when operating with EVPN-VxLAN type5 overlay ECMP at high tunnel next hop scale, the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) crash when a memory corruption issue is observed due to a buffer overflow that leads to corruption of heap management structures. This corrupted metadata is detected by the memory manager when later heap allocation or free operations are invoked, resulting in a reported heap corruption condition.

items.synopsis: On all branch SRX platforms (SRX300/320/340/345/380) running on FreeBSD12 OS, any upgrade post 24.4 release will cause a delay in every CLI (Command Line Interface) commit, with no impact to traffic forwarding or…
items.description: On all branch SRX platforms (SRX300/320/340/345/380) running on FreeBSD12 OS, any upgrade post 24.4 release will cause a delay in every CLI (Command Line Interface) commit, with no impact to traffic forwarding or network services.

items.synopsis: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when copying a file to a remote host using a hostname, the device is unable to resolve the hostname, causing the file transfer to fail.
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when copying a file to a remote host using a hostname, the device is unable to resolve the hostname, causing the file transfer to fail. Secure Copy (SCP) operations are not affected and continue to work as expected. This issue does not impact network services or device functionality.

items.synopsis: On MX304, MX301 and MX10K with LC4800 or LC9600 platforms, when the st0 interface is a part of ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi-Path) next-hop, the next hop corresponding to st0 interface will not be selected for traffic…
items.description: On MX304, MX301 and MX10K with LC4800 or LC9600 platforms, when the st0 interface is a part of ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi-Path) next-hop, the next hop corresponding to st0 interface will not be selected for traffic forwarding, because st0 will be marked as down resulting in functionality impact of ECMP. However, if there is a non-st0 as a backup link, this link will be selected for traffic forwarding. This doesn't impact IPSec traffic forwarded on this st0 interface.

items.synopsis: Event script failure occurs during a virtual chassis primary role change when the system is unable to load a required component at the time the script is executed.
items.description: Event script failure occurs during a virtual chassis primary role change when the system is unable to load a required component at the time the script is executed.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: Resolved an issue where configuration commits could intermittently fail when applying certain routing policy changes.
items.description: Resolved an issue where configuration commits could intermittently fail when applying certain routing policy changes. The problem occurred only under specific conditions during commit processing and could result in the commit operation aborting unexpectedly. This fix improves commit stability when updating routing policies.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms with virtual chassis (VC) deployments when the CLI command 'test configuration ' is executed it fails consistently and error messages are observed.
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms with virtual chassis (VC) deployments when the CLI command 'test configuration ' is executed it fails consistently and error messages are observed.

items.synopsis: On Junos Evolved platforms, a gNMI Get request for the OpenConfig root (origin: openconfig, type CONFIG) returns a NOT_FOUND error when only root-level OpenConfig metadata is configured and no OpenConfig configuration…
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms, a gNMI Get request for the OpenConfig root (origin: openconfig, type CONFIG) returns a NOT_FOUND error when only root-level OpenConfig metadata is configured and no OpenConfig configuration data nodes are present. In this scenario, the configured OpenConfig metadata is not returned unless at least one OpenConfig configuration subtree exists.

items.synopsis: On SRX platforms, upgrading from Junos OS releases later than 22.2 but earlier than 24.4 causes Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) Virtual Private Network (VPN) renegotiation during the first configuration commit after…
items.description: On SRX platforms, upgrading from Junos OS releases later than 22.2 but earlier than 24.4 causes Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) Virtual Private Network (VPN) renegotiation during the first configuration commit after reboot. Existing Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) VPN tunnels briefly disconnect and reconnect because retained Unified Threat Management (UTM) runtime warning data created by earlier software releases is processed differently by newer software versions. VPN traffic recovers automatically after renegotiation, and subsequent commits are not impacted.

items.synopsis: On MX10004 and MX10008 platforms, a rare timingd internal event-processing issue prevent PTP (Precision Time Protocol) synchronization from initializing successfully.
items.description: On MX10004 and MX10008 platforms, a rare timingd internal event-processing issue prevent PTP (Precision Time Protocol) synchronization from initializing successfully. When this condition occurs, PTP remains in the initializing state, PTP packet processing does not occur, and PTP Rx/Tx statistics remain at zero despite valid configuration and operational SyncE/ESMC (Ethernet Synchronization Messaging Channel) synchronization. The timingd process continues running, but internal timing events are no longer processed correctly, resulting in loss of PTP functionality until service recovery actions are performed. This issue does not impact normal data forwarding traffic and is limited to PTP operation.

items.category: usf flow and datapath issue on SPC3
items.synopsis: On Junos OS MX240/MX480/MX960 platforms with MX-SPC3 cards, the flowd process crash and reboots the service PIC when a stale IPv4 session is mistakenly reused for IPv6 due to a memory issue.
items.description: On Junos OS MX240/MX480/MX960 platforms with MX-SPC3 cards, the flowd process crash and reboots the service PIC when a stale IPv4 session is mistakenly reused for IPv6 due to a memory issue. During process restart the services remain down, session information is briefly lost and active traffic will drop, however the system recovers automatically.

items.synopsis: The nsd process unexpectedly crashes and restarts under heavy DNS-based address-book churn
items.description: On SRX Series devices running the 32-bit Network Security Daemon (nsd) with security policies referencing large numbers of Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) (dns-name) address-book objects, continuous high-frequency Domain Name System (DNS) activity causes memory exhaustion within the process over time. Once memory is depleted, the nsd process terminates unexpectedly with a crash and restarts.

items.synopsis: Junos Evolved platfrom, when gNMI collecting data from "optics/lanediags/lane/lane_laser_receiver_power_dbm" and "optics/lanediags/lane/lane_laser_output_power_dbm" are unreadable
items.description: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) encoding of leafs of type "ieeefloat32"([https://github.com/openconfig/public/blob/master/release/models/types/openconfig-types.yang#L127)](https://github.com/openconfig/public/blob/master/release/models/types/openconfig-types.yang#L127)) is not correct, causing gRPC Network Management Interface (gNMI) data outputs unreadable.

items.synopsis: New subscriber login request failure is seen due to missing PFE readiness update after boot
items.description: On MX240, MX480, MX960, MX2008, MX2010, MX2020 platforms with MPC2/3/4/5/6/7/8/9 line cards, the new subscriber login request will fail if subscriber login request is initiated when PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) is booting.

items.synopsis: Incorrect VRF label allocation for IPv4 L3VPN routes with RIB-Export leading to unexpected forwarding behaviour
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) VPN (Virtual Private Network) routes in a VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding instance) will be advertised with per-next-hop label, while IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) VPN routes in the same VRF correctly advertise VRF table-label. Under these combined conditions, IPv4 VPN routes are assigned per-next-hop labels instead of using a single shared VRF table-label, resulting in undesirable forwarding behaviour for IPv4 VPN routes.

items.synopsis: PFE disabled due to FIFO overflow
items.description: On Junos OS MX304 and MX10004/MX10008 routers with Line Card (LC) LC4800/LC9600, the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) gets disabled. When the Logical Unified Scheduler Subsystem (LUSS) Packet Processing Engines (PPEs) were busy, the On-Chip Gigabit Ethernet (OGE) traffic was starved for an extended duration, which resulted in a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) buffer overflow. If traffic is flowing while the Flexible PIC Concentrator (FPC) is coming online, a FIFO overflow interrupt is triggered, which causes the PFE to be disabled.

items.synopsis: [MX304] Certain 'cat' commands within the 'show vmhost support-info' command in RSI try to access files that are not present on the MX304, causing error messages to appear.
items.description: As part of the RSI process, execute the "show vmhost support-info" command to comprehensively collect the vmhost logs using various cat commands. Some of these commands attempt to access files that do not exist on the MX304, leading to error messages.

items.synopsis: On MX304 platforms, error logs are seen after reboot, due to a missing file presence check
items.description: On MX304 platforms, repeated error messages are observed in Linux (jncl) logs after a reboot. The issue occurs when a shell script attempts to read the non-existent sysfs file: cat: /sys/devices/virtual/net/macvtap0/statistics/rx_errors There is no traffic or service impact.

items.synopsis: EVPN-VXLAN: Duplicate Proxied Neighbor Advertisements Missing Router/Override Flags Disrupt IPv6 Connectivity
items.description: When Junos and Junos Evolved platform sends two proxied Neighbor Advertisement for default gateway, second one without Router flag and target Link-Layer address. The second Neighbor Advertisement can disrupt connectivity for end hosts. A proxied Neighbor Advertisement (NA) is an IPv6 mechanism where a network device responds to Neighbor Discovery requests on behalf of another device, instead of the actual endpoint replying itself.

items.synopsis: Traffic drops observed on MX304 due to LMIC restart/swap causing policer address collision across PFE partitions
items.description: On MX304 platforms, when an LMIC (Line-Card Module Interface Card) restart/swap occurs and firewall filters with interface or ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) policers are applied across interfaces belonging to two different LMICs, a policer address collision across PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) partitions occurs, leading to discard filter installation and resulting in traffic drops until the FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) is restarted to restore normal forwarding.

items.synopsis: dscp-code-point under host-outbound-traffic is not enabled on PTX
items.description: set class-of-service host-outbound-traffic dscp-code-point was disabled on PTX in 25.4R1. Later it was enabled in 26.2R1 and backported to 25.4R2

items.synopsis: ARP and MAC/IP table for virtual IP mac is not installed in bridge domain which is part if EVPN instance
items.description: In all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms supporting EVPN-MPLS, EVPN-VXLAN when VRRP device is connected to EVPN PE with Aggregate Ethernet interface the VRRP virtual IP may fail to install ARP and destination route entries when the VRRP virtual MAC is learned on one FPC while the ARP response is received on another FPC with a source MAC mismatch.

items.synopsis: IP allocation failure in EVPN-MPLS/VXLAN environments due to incorrect Proxy ARP responses
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms running a release from 25.4R1 in an EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network)-MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching ) or EVPN-VXLAN (Virtual Extensible Local Area Network) environment, with an IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) interface configured as the Layer 3 gateway, when ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) probe packets are received while proxy ARP is enabled, the device generates proxy ARP replies for unresolved IP (Internet Protocol) addresses. This causes false duplicate IP detection and leads to DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) address assignment failure.

items.synopsis: runt, fragment and jabber counters are not incrementing on EX4300-MPs
items.description: runt, fragment and jabber counters are not incrementing on EX4300-MPs

items.synopsis: PoE outage observed on EX4400 in a rare scenario
items.description: On EX4400 platforms, loss of PoE (Power over Ethernet) power is seen on ports after port bounce or even during normal operation without specific external trigger . This causes outage on all PoE ports and devices connected to PoE port will not receive power causing service impact.

items.synopsis: The dcpfe process crash is seen on QFX10002-60C platforms during high frequency route churn
items.description: On QFX10002-60C platforms in an Ethernet Virtual Private Network (EVPN) Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (VxLAN) setup, the dcpfe process crash is seen, causing the Flexible PIC Concentrator (FPC) to restart and thus impacts forwarding traffic. This is a rare occurrence when Layer 3 traffic is forwarded through an EVPN VxLAN type-5 tunnel and continuous route churn (route add/delete operations) is in progress.

items.synopsis: LDP-IGP synchronization remains stuck in holddown state on ISIS multiinstance interfaces
items.description: When the ldp-synchronization statement is configured under ISIS multiinstance interfaces, the router might fail to properly synchronize LDP (Label Distribution Protocol) with ISIS during adjacency establishment. As a result, the ISIS interface remains in the LDP synchronization holddown state, and the advertised ISIS metric is not updated as expected. This may lead to suboptimal routing or traffic forwarding inconsistencies.

items.synopsis: DHCPv6 Relay Active Leasequery not able to establish TCP session to peer
items.description: On all MX platforms, when configuring Dual Stack DHCPv6 ALQ without configuring DHCPv4 ALQ (active-leasequery), the ALQ will not be able to establish the TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) session for the ALQ peer due to XID (Exchange Identification) mismatch. This can lead to DHCPv6 subscriber bindings sync issue and server ALQ, resulting in compromising the redundancy functionality.

items.synopsis: The dhcpd crash triggered by DHCPv6 ALQ peer state inconsistency
items.description: On MX104, MX204, MX240, MX301, MX304, MX480, MX960, MX2008, MX2010, MX2020, MX10003, MX10004, MX10008 and MX10016 platforms DHCPv6 (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol version 6) ALQ (Active Lease Query) peer state inconsistency creates an invalid subscriber entry for a bound IPv6 address, resulting in a jdhcpd (Junos DHCP daemon) crash with recurring core dumps and subscriber traffic impact.

items.category: Adresses ALG issues found in JSF
items.synopsis: SIP calls may not function properly in the SIP ALG application on MX-SPC3 and SRX platforms
items.description: On MX platforms with SPC3 line-cards/ SRX platforms, when there are bandwidth attributes carried in SDP(Session Description Protocol) messages inside SIP(Session Initiation Protocol) packets, SIP application traffic and SIP calls get impacted.

items.category: interfaces and zones for junos js software
items.synopsis: MRU not updating when mtu is configured on SRX SFP28 pic with interface speed configuration
items.description: On SRX1600/SRX2300/SRX4300 platforms, the Maximum Receive Unit (MRU) does not update correctly when a non-default Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) value is configured on an interface belonging to an SFP28 Physical Interface Card (PIC) while port speed is explicitly configured at the interface level. Incorrect MRU programming results in packet size inconsistencies, which lead to traffic drops for packets exceeding the incorrectly programmed MRU value.

items.synopsis: NSD main thread delay during policy file serialization on SRX5K platforms leads to instability
items.description: On SRX5K platforms, during policy configuration processing using the policy file serialization feature, the Network Security Daemon (NSD) main thread can stop yielding for more than one second. This results in warning messages in system logs and can impact protocol/FPC stability if the delay becomes excessive.

items.synopsis: SRX400 Series J-Web does not display system message logs
items.description: On SRX400 Series platforms, system message logs are not displayed in J-Web under Monitor > Log > System for any selected time range. The log entries remain available through the Junos OS Evolved command-line interface (CLI). This issue has no traffic impact and no other functional impact.

items.synopsis: The /interfaces/interface/state/enabled/ does not export all interfaces under a single wrap
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC1-11, LC2301/LC9600, LC4800 and MX304, when subscribed to the OpenConfig gNMI sensor /interfaces/interface/state/enabled/ with a 60-second sample interval, an incomplete data delivery at collector is observed when the device is deployed with 2 or more line cards.

items.category: Port-based link layer security services and protocols that a
items.synopsis: MACsec traffic encryption/decryption failure post SFP OIR with interface and session in up state
items.description: On MX301 platform, After SFP (Small Form-factor Pluggable transceiver) Online Insertion and Removal (OIR) on a MACsec (Media Access Control Security) enabled interface, the link and MACsec session remain UP, but MACsec encryption and decryption stop functioning. This results in traffic loss and causes service impact.

items.synopsis: MX platforms with MPC10 and PPPoE subscribers can experience egress traffic black holing after WAN link flap events
items.description: On MX Series routers equipped with MPC10 cards and high scale PPPoE (Point to Point Protocol over Ethernet) subscriber deployments, a WAN (Wide Area Networks) interface link flap under active traffic conditions can cause corruption of internal scheduler credits. When this occurs, Packet Forwarding Engine queue flush operations can fail and subscriber egress traffic can become permanently black holed. Symptoms include "cannot Free L1/L2/L3/L4 node" messages, and queue flush failures. The issue is more likely to occur on interfaces carrying significant subscriber traffic and repeated link flap events.

items.synopsis: Disabling one port in the breakout port channel makes another port down
items.description: On all Junos MX platform, when MPC10E interfaces use breakout cabling, administratively disabling one breakout port may unexpectedly impact another port within the same MAC quad due to nondeterministic breakout initialization.

items.category: MPC11 ULC platform software related issues.
items.synopsis: JDI-RCT:M/Mx: ISIS session over MPC11 cards flapped due to "3-Way handshake failed" during ISSU (FRU upgrade stage - reboot phase)
items.description: JDI-RCT:M/Mx: ISIS session over MPC11 cards flapped due to "3-Way handshake failed" during ISSU (FRU upgrade stage - reboot phase)

items.synopsis: High CPU utilization of the acx-arm-feb process on ACX710 platforms after upgrade or reboot when Precision Time Protocol (PTP) or Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE) is configured
items.description: On ACX710 platforms running Junos OS, the acx-arm-feb process reaches 100 percent CPU utilization after a system upgrade or reboot when Precision Time Protocol (PTP) or Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE) is configured and the associated interfaces are enabled. This condition results in control plane degradation and traffic impact.

items.synopsis: FTP passive mode fails on Junos platforms
items.description: On all Junos platforms, FTP ( File transfer protocol ) sessions using PASV mode fail. As a result, customers relying on PASV for fetching operational scripts experienced transfer failures. Impact included blocked transfers.

items.category: vpls on branch (jseries and srx) platforms
items.synopsis: ISIS adjacency not coming up on SRX 3XX series platforms in VPLS topology
items.description: On SRX 3XX platforms, due to incorrect mbuf (Memory Buffer) allocation, the ISIS (Intermediate System-to-Intermediate System) packets with MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) tag transiting over a L2VPN (Layer 2 Virtual Private Network) are dropped if the packet size exceeds 1500 bytes resulting in the ISIS adjacency remaining stuck in the initializing state, leading to routing issues. This issue is intermittent and observed only when the SRX 3XX device is serving as the PE in MPLS L2VPN network.

items.synopsis: Removal of the flexible-match-range from CLI, as it is not supported
items.description: On Junos QFX5100, QFX5200, and QFX5210, the unsupported knob "flexible-match-range" under "ethernet-switching"is hidden from the CLI.

items.synopsis: GBP tag is not getting applied from prefix list when IPV4 or IPV6 address crosses certain limit
items.description: On EX4100, EX4400, EX4650 & QFX5120 platforms having GBP configured in an EVPN-VXLAN setup it is observed that when IPV4 or IPV6 addresses in prefix-list crosses certain limit (for IPv4 is 8 or 9 depending on character width and for IPV6 limit is towards character length of buffer being 192 character width, with approx count 3 or 4) inconsistency is seen in the tagging behavior where some of the IP tags is not reflected. As a result this affects the policy and it does not work as per expectation. There is no traffic impact due to this issue.

items.synopsis: ARP is not resolved on directly connected interface of Junos QFX5K platform enabled with Spanning Tree protocol
items.description: On the Junos QFX5K platform, when any Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) variant, such as STP, RSTP, MSTP, or VSTP, is enabled, ARP is not resolved on QFX5K interfaces if the interface is configured with flexible VLAN tagging and Enterprise (EP) or Service Provider (SP) style configuration. As a result, IP traffic is lost over the affected interfaces.

items.synopsis: QFX5110 incorrectly converts untagged native VLAN traffic to tagged traffic on VXLAN egress
items.description: On QFX5110 platforms running Junos OS, when Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN), flexible-vlan-tagging, vlan-id-list, native-vlan-id, and encapsulate-inner-vlan are configured together using a Service Provider (SP)-style configuration, untagged ingress traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated with an unexpected Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) tag. As a result, the remote VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint (VTEP) receives the traffic as tagged instead of untagged, which can lead to end-to-end traffic loss.

items.synopsis: In the EVPN VXLAN scenario restart routing causes multicast traffic disruption
items.description: On Junos OS EX and QFX platforms, a routing process restart in an Ethernet VPN (EVPN) Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) environment results in multicast traffic disruption due to the loss of multicast forwarding state on the Designated Forwarder (DF) switch.

items.category: QFX5K JUNOS Interface, MACSec, Optics, SDK, PHY
items.synopsis: The dcpfe process crash observed during a system reboot or PFE restart when software-based linkscan is configured
items.description: On QFX5120-48Y, QFX5120-48T, QFX5120-32C and EX4650 platforms, a system reboot or PFE restart after configuring software-based linkscan causes the dcpfe process to crash. As a result, traffic forwarding on interfaces associated with the affected FPC will be temporarily impacted during the recovery period.

items.category: RPD infrastructure issues related to NSR, GRES, switchover,
items.synopsis: rpd crash caused by stale deleted tunnel entry
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, deleting a tunnel leaves its entry on the systems processing list instead of removing it. When the system later references this stale entry, it results in a crash. This issue is specific to APP-based dynamic tunnels.

items.category: RPD Next-hop issues including indirect, CNH, and MCNH
items.synopsis: In Class-Based Forwarding with ECMP scenario traffic gets dropped due to incorrect next-hop handling process in PFE programming
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms where CBF (Class-Based Forwarding) and ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi Path) is configured and in non - MPLS (Multi-Protocol Label Switching) based IP traffic forwarding scenario, packet loss can be observed due to next-hop process handling in PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) programming for indexed next-hop installation by CBF.

items.category: RPD route tables, resolver, routing instances, static routes
items.synopsis: The rpd process crash during RIB reconfiguration causing routing session resets and reconvergence
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, the rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) process crashes during RIB (Routing Information Base)-export configuration reconfiguration involving BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) routing policies, causing routing session flaps and routing reconvergence.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes during repeated RSVP session clear operations
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, the rpd process crashes when Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) sessions are repeatedly cleared under specific timing conditions. This issue occurs due to a timing window during RSVP processing on the standby Routing Engine (RE) while sessions are being re-established, which results in an invalid memory access and leads to an the rpd process crashes.

items.synopsis: RSVP detour LSP does not follow configured FRR admin-group exclusion constraints
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching), RSVP (Resource Reservation Protocol), dynamic tunnels, and an LSP (Label-Switched Path) template with FRR (Fast Reroute) admin-group exclusion constraints are configured, the detour LSP does not follow the configured exclusions after the primary LSP becomes unavailable. The detour LSP uses an unintended path, while traffic and services remain unaffected.

items.category: Issues related to broadband edge apps (PPP, DHCP) on Trio ch
items.synopsis: FPC crash triggered by peer member restart in AE bundle
items.description: On Junos MX platforms with line card scale, and subscriber over AE (Aggregated Ethernet) is enabled, if one FPC hosting an AE member link restarts, another FPC hosting a different member link of the same AE bundle will crash. When the crash occur, PFEMAN is stuck for more than 240 seconds and traffic loss will occur on the affected FPCs.

items.synopsis: FPC major alarm triggered by AE member link flaps resulting in PFE being disabled
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC7E/MPC8E/MPC9E/MPC10E/MPC11E/LC9600 line cards or an MX304 platform, The PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) is disabled following a Major alarm on the FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator), when the error message "XQSS_CMERROR_DSTAT_INT_REG_DROP0_VOTE_OVRN" is triggered after a member link of an AE (Aggregated Ethernet) interface flaps, resulting in traffic impact on the affected PFE.

items.category: Trio pfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: Multicast traffic disruption on VLAN after CoS configuration changes
items.description: On MX platforms , multicast traffic over VLAN interfaces (IRB) will be impacted after certain CoS (Class Of Service) configuration changes. This can result in multicast traffic not reaching downstream receivers.

items.synopsis: MAC RADIUS CoA requests fail when the RADIUS server uses a management routing instance on Junos platforms
items.description: On all Junos platforms, when Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) is configured for IEEE 802.1X Media Access Control (MAC) RADIUS authentication and Change of Authorization (CoA) is used, if the RADIUS server is configured to use a management routing instance, CoA requests are not acknowledged and dynamic session updates such as IP address assignment and session timeout changes fail.

items.synopsis: Traffic drops observed when using url-category without web filtering profile on Junos SRX Platforms
items.description: On Junos SRX platforms, when only url-category is configured in policy (without web-filter policy), the packet handler continues to receive packets while the session is in HELD state, causing subsequent packets to be dropped.

items.synopsis: The smdp process crash is observed on MX Aggregation Device during Junos upgrade in a Junos Fusion Deployment
items.description: In all Junos MX platforms acting as the AD (Aggregation Device) in a Junos Fusion deployment, a Junos software upgrade causes the smdp (Satellite Platform and Management Daemon) process to crash impacting forwarding plane services. This issue is observed when AD nodes are moved to a higher Junos version while the SD (Satellite nodes) are still running a lower version.

items.synopsis: vSRX3.0 connectivity loss and service disruption due to traffic interruption during processing delays
items.description: On Junos OS vSRX3.0 platforms, two issues have been addressed. The first issue is related to flow control configured; connectivity loss and service disruption will be observed when the device experiences processing delays that can interrupt incoming network traffic. The issue affects critical control protocols such as BFD and BGP. The second issue is a CPU (Central Processing Unit) utilization display issue, where the show chassis routing-engine command reports CPU utilization for CPU0 only instead of showing the average utilization across all Routing Engine CPUs; this is a display-only issue.
